item.title: Barca hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
item.description: Giuliano Simeone was on target for Atletico Madrid as they beat Levante to move provisionally top of La Liga on Saturday (JOSE JORDAN) Raphinha and Lamine Yamal struck twice each as Barcelona thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more. Raphinha netted twice in the first half, either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. There was a minute's silence at the start of each of the day's matches in memory of the 69 victims of the train crash in the province of Toledo that rocked Spain this week. Flick lined up with Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong playing at centre-back and youngster Brian Farinas making his first start at right-back, amid a spate of defensive injuries. It did not hamper the champions. Barcelona moved ahead in the eighth minute, with La Liga's top scorer Raphinha continuing his red-hot form. Midfield maestro Pedri played in Lopez, who pulled the ball across for the Brazil international to bundle home. Alaves came close through Abde Rebbach before Lopez doubled Barcelona's lead in the 23rd minute. Yamal slipped the midfielder in and, from a tight angle, Lopez smashed the ball across goal and fortuitously in at the far post, seemingly intending to cross it. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Perhaps frustrated by his miss, Yamal smashed home the fourth with an instinctive low strike from the edge of the box in first half stoppage time. Adeyemi blazed another presentable chance over the crossbar early in the second half after Lopez unselfishly set him up. Yamal got Barca's fifth with a neat dink over the goalkeeper after substitute Gabriel Jesus played him through on goal. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. - Seven in a row - Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Earlier Atletico Madrid, second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved back two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou. Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend's La Liga home Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick's side found their groove once more. Teenage winger Yamal netted again midway through the second half and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca's sixth, before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves. Karim Adeyemi and Yamal both missed glorious chances from close range to expand on Barca's lead, with Raphinha showing the duo how to do it as he bagged his 15th league goal. Lopez sent the forward through on goal and Raphinha produced a lethal finish across Antonio Sivera. Gordon produced a similar finish for Barca's sixth and the only tarnish on their evening was former Real Madrid striker Diaz netting late on. - Seven in a row - Earlier in Valencia Diego Simeone's Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante. Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions. "I'm very happy with the team's work," Atletico coach Simeone told Movistar. "We're very far from the end of the season... we'll keep going game by game." Alex Baena, the visitors' main creative outlet, set up both goals as Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club's record set by Luis Aragones. "I don't feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years," said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011. Atletico host Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Barca to the Metropolitano stadium next weekend in La Liga. On Sunday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, third, visit Racing Santander among other fixtures. rbs/nf/dmc

item.title: Fort Collins boys surge to 3rd place at Colorado state cross-country
item.description: Another strong Fort Collins-area high cross-country season wrapped with an elite finish at the Colorado state meet. Fort Collins High School's Will Johns led a Lambkins surge, racing to third place in Class 5A boys as an individual and spurring the team to an impressive bronze finish Oct. 31 at Colorado Springs' Norris Penrose Event Center. Johns surged in the race's final portion, running the final 1.05 miles in a hair over 5 minutes. He crossed the finish line in 15:12.44, moving up from 12th to fifth to third throughout the race. The junior was just one second behind the runner-up and sixteen back of 5A boys champion Abdinasir Hassan from Northfield. Johns capped a phenomenal season as one of the state's top runners. He finished top-five in every Colorado event this season and won the Front Range League championship. Sean Giles was the next-best finisher from Fort Collins, taking 12th in 15:55.68. Fort Collins won a close race for third in the team standings, finishing with 156 points. That was just one ahead of Heritage (157) and two clear of Mountain Vista (158). Niwot was well clear, winning the 5A title with a mere 60 points. It was a fantastic showing for the Lambkins against an elite field that got even better with state power Niwot moving up to Class 5A. Here are the other Fort Collins scorers for the third-place squad: Owen Kirkpatrick (37th, 16:32.80) Oliver Singleton, (55th, 16:48.00) Tobin Rapley, (59th, 16:52.70) Fort Collins also had the top local team finish in the 5A girls race, finishing eighth with 270 points. These Lambkins girls placed in the top 50 runners: Brooke Johns (30th, 19:14.52) Emma Jones (37th, 19:24.68) Olive Giuliani (40th, 19:33.61) The Fossil Ridge girls finished 10th as a team in Class 5A with a pair of top-50 placers: Avery Breitigam (13th, 18:46.05) Maya DiGiallonardo (47th, 19:43.65) Rocky Mountain freshman Jordyn Grossnickle took 20th among 5A girls in 19:01.19. Rigby Ruffer led the Lobos in the 5A boys race, taking 30th in 16:22.40. Heritage Christian girls grab 3rd in Class 2A The Eagles finished third in a tight 2A girls team race, scoring 80 points to finish just five points back of champion Thomas Maclaren School (75) and two off runner-up Ridgway (78). Kate Lukens led the way with a second straight podium finish at state, placing ninth in 20:08.46. Heritage Christian's depth shone through, with all five Eagles scorers finishing inside the 2A girls top 50: Emma Lukens (30th, 21:17.11) Hailey Lukens (40th, 21:42.28) Maebelle Cheney (45th, 21:52.54) Elyse Robinson (50th, 22:07.03) HCA also earned a podium spot in the 2A boys race, with Lucas Delorme crossing in eighth in 16:50.25. Timnath leads local 4A finishers It wasn't a third straight title, but the Cubs had the only podium finisher among local runners. item.title: Julian Nagelsmann has already received Juventus’ call, INEOS need to act soon
item.description: Julian Nagelsmann has already received Juventus’ call, INEOS need to act soon Despite their disastrous run of form, Manchester United decided to stick with Michael Carrick following extensive crisis talks. There were murmurs that football director Jason Wilcox had approached Eddie Howe , but those reports proved premature as the former United midfielder remained at the helm . That decision has not worked out well, as the Red Devils lost 2-0 to Chelsea on Saturday. The first half was a more cohesive performance , but Lisandro Martinez single-handedly lost United the game . While Carrick November international break begins . Nagelsmann is a wanted man Recruitment chief Christopher Vivell has been advocating for Julian Nagelsmann, but the former Germany coach is a wanted man. RB Leipzig and Fenerbahce have been linked with the ex-Bayern Munich boss, and Juventus have now joined the race. According to journalist Rudy Galetti , “Juventus have just contacted Julian Nagelsmann, adding the German coach to their preferred alternatives should they decide to replace Spalletti. “The former Germany boss is weighing several options for his future and appreciated the Bianconeri’s approach.” Why INEOS are delaying the final call As things stand, Julian Nagelsmann seems to be slipping away from United’s grasp. But not everyone in the hierarchy would be too concerned about the loss. Many want the club to show some ambition and try to bring in project managers such as Cesc Fabregas or Unai Emery . Both are unlikely to make the jump mid-season, so a decision might have to wait for now. With Howe’s compensation claims set to reduce further and the current head coach ‘s break clause also due to activate, the penny-pinching co-owners have a choice to make. online polls

item.title: Prayers Pour In as Arizona Wide Receiver Carted Off the Field After Nasty Hit Against Texas Tech
item.description: Copyright: xx ZUMA-20221015_zaf_c04_276.jpg SeanxBrownx csmphototwo980630 ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Big 12 showdown between the Texas Tech Red Raiders and Arizona Wildcats was arguably one of Week 9’s most consequential games, but the action took a worrying turn in the third quarter. Arizona lost 34-26 to Texas Tech on Saturday, and in the third quarter, wide receiver R.J. Mosley suffered what looked like a knee injury. It happened on third-and-18, when Mosley caught a pass from quarterback Noah Fifita and was brought down by Texas Tech defensive back Amier Boyd after an eight-yard gain. Wildcats fans quickly sent prayers his way. The moment he landed, Mosley reached for his knee, and Fifita and a number of Arizona players rushed to respond. The broadcast footage shared by ESPN College Football X handle showed a horrific injury, with his knee seemingly dislocated or potentially broken. ESPN’s broadcast skipped the replay because the production truck decided the footage was too graphic to air. Wildcats players immediately gathered around their injured teammate as medical personnel stabilized his leg. Mosley was loaded onto a cart and taken off the field as the crowd watched in silence before applauding. He was seen smiling as he left. A devastating moment has shaken college football. Stay informed on Arizona's injury updates and game impact with EssentiallySports' latest coverage. The severity of the injury was enough to leave even seasoned insiders deeply concerned about the freshman wide receiver’s well-being. One insider couldn’t hide his concern, writing, “Oh man. Bad-looking leg injury for talented freshman wideout R.J. Mosley. You know it’s not good when they won’t show a replay.” Once it was clear how serious the injury looked, Arizona fans turned to social media to support the freshman receiver, posting prayers and messages of encouragement. A fan shared the video and wrote a heartfelt message, “Praying for RJ Mosley.” Another joined and sent prayers, writing, “Prayers to R.J. Mosley what a brutal-looking injury.” Fifita dropped to a knee and prayed as medical staff rushed to Mosley. The crowd watched in silence before erupting into applause as Mosley was carted off the field. The sight of teammates and players surrounding Mosley following the injury was heartbreaking, but for some fans, the scene itself raised serious concerns about the gravity of the situation. One fan pointed to the worrying image, writing, “Guys huddling up around him before the cart tells you enough. that’s never the scene you want to see” Others put their concerns aside to send their support and prayers to the injured wide receiver. One fan shared an emotional message, “SENDING PRAYERS AND HUGS TO U OF A RJ MOSLEY. 🌹” Taylor McGregor, ESPN’s sideline reporter, relayed early in the fourth quarter that Mosley was undergoing lower-body X-rays as medical staff worked to size up the injury. He was subsequently taken to a local hospital for further examination and treatment

item.title: 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw slapped with hefty fine for punching Falcons’ Drake London
item.description: 49ers star linebacker Dre Greenlaw has had a costly start to the season. NFL insider Tom Pelissero broke news on Saturday that Greenlaw has been fined $12,537 for unnecessary roughness against Falcons star wide receiver Drake London . Dre Greenlaw of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sideline during a game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, California, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. Getty Images Greenlaw tried to punch the ball out of London’s hands during the 49ers’ 29-20 loss to the Falcons last Sunday. Greenlaw’s punch missed its target, as he connected with London’s helmet instead. San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw loading up to punch the ball out of Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London’s hands. (X/@TomPelissero). No penalty was called on Greenlaw during the play, but video replays of the incident showed why Greenlaw ultimately got in trouble. London left the game to be evaluated for a concussion after the punch but was ultimately cleared and able to return. Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) walks off the field after a game against the San Francisco 49ers in Atlanta, Georgia, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is no reason to believe there was any malice behind Greenlaw’s punch, as it just didn’t connect where it was meant to. Greenlaw was fined $11,941 by the NFL for taunting the Broncos’ bench (specifically his former head coach, Sean Payton) earlier in the season. The star linebacker will surely hope to stop giving the league reasons to fine him once San Francisco returns from its bye week.

item.title: Barcelona star bags his first-ever assist for the club vs Alavés
item.description: Barcelona star bags his first-ever assist for the club vs Alavés A member of the midfield ranks at La Liga giants Barcelona on Saturday hit a long-awaited personal benchmark in the club’s colours. This came upon Rodri breaking his duck in the assists column in Blaugrana colours. Barcelona were of course back in action a short time ago, welcoming Deportivo Alavés to Catalunya’s capital for a league clash. Hansi Flick’s troops headed into proceedings desperate for a bounce-back result, following back-to-back defeats across all competitions. And when all was said and done, this is precisely what they managed, courtesy of a 6-1 romp. The aforementioned Rodri featured from the off in the fixture, from his berth at the base of midfield. And as alluded to above, during the 2nd-half, the 30-year-old hit a personal milestone for his new club. After laying on Anthony Gordon’s late 6th, Rodri registered his first-ever assist in the famed red and blue of Barcelona. Conor Laird – GSFN

And as alluded to above, during the 2nd-half, the 30-year-old hit a personal milestone for his new club. After laying on Anthony Gordon’s late 6th, Rodri registered his first-ever assist in the famed red and blue of Barcelona. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Suzuki's costly mistake as Villa draw with Fulham
item.description: Premier League Aston Villa 1 - 1 Fulham FT Aston Villa are unbeaten in their past five Premier League matches [Getty Images] Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropped the ball into his own net as Fulham had a helping hand in recovering to earn a Premier League draw at Villa Park. Striker Nicolas Jackson had earlier continued his fine scoring form for the hosts, but his first-half goal was not enough for victory because of Suzuki's costly error. The Japan international could not hold on to Alex Iwobi's inswinging corner midway through the second half and fumbled the ball narrowly over the line for an own goal. Villa were in good shape when Jackson got his sixth goal in all competitions in October - more than any other top-flight player. He raced on to Johan Manzambi's pass, evaded weak challenges from David Affengruber and Timothy Castagne, and slotted past Bernd Leno. That goal came in the 39th minute, and Villa should have gone ahead 23 minutes earlier when they were awarded a penalty. Leon Goretzka's header was handled by Sander Berge, with referee Sam Barrott originally missing the offence, only for video assistant referee Matthew Donohue to advise him to watch it n a pitchside monitor. Barrott changed his decision, but Villa captain John McGinn could not capitalise as his penalty bounced away off the crossbar. When it was goalless, Fulham nearly went ahead when Suzuki made a superb one-handed save to keep out Oscar Bobb's effort. Suzuki also denied Gonzalo Garcia in the second half, but he badly blundered for the equaliser and it ultimately proved costly for the hosts. Villa have now won three, drawn three and lost three of their nine league matches and are ninth in the table, three points and six places above Fulham in 15th. More to follow. Have your say on Aston Villa's display What did you make of Fulham's perfomance?

item.title: UFC Vegas 123 live results, highlights, play-by-play
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Oct. 31, 2026) with UFC Halloween (a.k.a. UFC Vegas 123 ) , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event goes down inside the familiar META APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada. Our main event on this Halloween event is Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan ( see betting odds here ). UFC Halloween Preview It feels a little odd to see a UFC fight night land on Halloween. It would be nice if UFC did something to dress up for the occasion, but knowing them it will probably be business as usual. Renato Moicano vs. Tom Nolan draw the short straw of being unable to go trick or treating with their kids this night ( are you? ). They are meeting in the main event, despite Moicano saying he was desperate to escape the APEX. UFC Halloween’s co-main event is DC’s boy Jacobe Smith taking on the veteran Randy Brown ( on super short notice ). Smith has decimated all who have stood in his way so far. If he runs through Brown, then he’s a real player at 170 pounds . Rounding out UFC Halloween’s main card is Ode’ Osbourne vs. Cody Durden , Yana Santos vs. Luana Santos and Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani vs. Farman Hasanov . The “Prelims” are headlined by Francis Marshall vs. Dakota Hope . The biggest match-up on that portion of the card is Zachary Reese vs. Mickey Gall , with Gall looking to avoid his fifth straight loss. Former OKTAGON two-division champ Lucia Szabova also debuts at this event. She fights Tainara Lisboa . The rest of undercard includes Rodrigo Sezinando vs. Theodor Berggren , Julian Erosa vs. Jeong Yeong Lee ( in a retirement fight for Juicy J ), Nick Klein vs. Joseph Kropschott and Talita Alencar vs. Piera Rodriguez . UFC Halloween Start Date and Time We are back in the APEX tonight and that means a return to our usual broadcast times. UFC Halloween “Prelims” will begin at 5 p.m. ET . UFC Halloween main card is scheduled to start at 8 p.m. ET . All of Halloween airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here . The live blog here starts rolling below at 5 p.m. ET . item.title: Moreira on best game ‘so far’ for Milan, while Pulisic is lucky charm against Inter
item.description: Moreira on best game ‘so far’ for Milan, while Pulisic is lucky charm against Inter Diego Moreira admits this was his best Milan performance ‘for now’ after a goal and two assists, while Christian Pulisic jokes about his incredible record against Inter. The Derby della Madonnina was dominated by the Rossoneri, who surged into a 2-0 lead in the opening 10 minutes thanks to the Pulisic header and Adrien Rabiot strike, both on assists from Diego Moreira. The Belgium international secured his Man of the Match status by getting on the scoresheet with a viciously dipping free kick in the 3-1 victory. Diego Moreira and Pulisic relish Milan night ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “I am very happy, with my teammates we did a great job, we fought to earn the three points,” Moreira told Sky Sport Italia. “We have to stay focused game by game, it’s still early in the season, we need to take it step by step. For now, it is my best game in the Milan shirt. For now.” Check the Football Italia Player Ratings for Milan 3-1 Inter ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Kaka was in the stands and inducted into the Milan Hall of Fame before kick-off, visibly moved to tears as he saluted the crowd. How did Moreira feel scoring in the derby with Kaka watching, wearing the same 22 jersey that the Brazilian had here? “Thank you for coming and giving me your shirt, I am very happy!” ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Christian Pulisic of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) This was the first Derby della Madonnina for Diego Moreira, but Pulisic is now an old hand at this fixture and opened the scoring within four minutes. “We started very strong with intensity, physicality, scored two goals and then the third before half-time. This victory is very important for us,” Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia. The American has scored in four editions of the derby and Milan won all of them, so is he their lucky charm? “I want to continue scoring goals in the derby, so that way we’ll win! These are three very important points, but we’ve got to find this consistency to play like this all the time. In the big games, it’s not a surprise that we do well.”

item.title: Steve O'Donnell Shuts Down NASCAR Buyout Speculation Amid Investors Circling Daytona Beach’s Door
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA – JUNE 21: NASCAR, Motorsport, USA CEO Steve ODonnell during the NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base event on Sunday June 21, 2026 at the Naval Base Coronado in San Diego, CA. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire AUTO: JUN 21 NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532606211036 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire NASCAR has spent nearly eight decades building a business that extends far beyond what happens on the racetrack. Its value stretches across television rights, iconic venues, sponsorships, and a loyal American fan base. With live sports becoming increasingly attractive to investors, the sanctioning body has reasons to draw attention from businesses looking for their next major opportunity. But there is a difference between wanting a piece of NASCAR’s commercial success and convincing the people who own it to surrender control. For the France family, that distinction is particularly important. NASCAR remains a privately held business, and outside interest inevitably raises questions about its long-term ownership. Whether the approaches represent an opportunity to bring fresh capital into the sport or the beginning of another takeover conversation is a different matter altogether. “For its part, the Daytona Beach-based governing body NASCAR has been on the receiving end of unsolicited approaches by businesses seeking equity in the company or to work on joint ventures, according to people familiar with the matter,” reported Sports Business Journal, according to SpeedFreaks . NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell has said that NASCAR is not for sale, and just because investors are showing interest does not mean any deal will happen. The distinction between an outright acquisition and an investment is central to the speculation. The reported approaches do not establish that NASCAR has received a formal takeover bid or started a sale process. Instead, they point towards businesses exploring minority ownership opportunities or joint ventures. Both could bring outside money into the organization without necessarily changing who controls it. NASCAR's leadership is drawing a clear line in the sand as major money circles the sport. Subscribe to stay ahead of what's really driving these pivotal negotiations. This is not the first time the France family has faced questions about selling. In 2018, NASCAR reportedly engaged Goldman Sachs to explore potential investment and ownership options. NBCUniversal emerged as a serious prospective buyer, with discussions involving a possible minority stake. item.content:encoded: SAN DIEGO, CA – JUNE 21: NASCAR, Motorsport, USA CEO Steve ODonnell during the NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base event on Sunday June 21, 2026 at the Naval Base Coronado in San Diego, CA. Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire AUTO: JUN 21 NASCAR Cup Series Anduril 250 Race the Base EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon9532606211036 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire NASCAR has spent nearly eight decades building a business that extends far beyond what happens on the racetrack. Its value stretches across television rights, iconic venues, sponsorships, and a loyal American fan base. With live sports becoming increasingly attractive to investors, the sanctioning body has reasons to draw attention from businesses looking for their next major opportunity. But there is a difference between wanting a piece of NASCAR’s commercial success and convincing the people who own it to surrender control. For the France family, that distinction is particularly important. NASCAR remains a privately held business, and outside interest inevitably raises questions about its long-term ownership. Whether the approaches represent an opportunity to bring fresh capital into the sport or the beginning of another takeover conversation is a different matter altogether. “For its part, the Daytona Beach-based governing body NASCAR has been on the receiving end of unsolicited approaches by businesses seeking equity in the company or to work on joint ventures, according to people familiar with the matter,” reported Sports Business Journal, according to SpeedFreaks . NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell has said that NASCAR is not for sale, and just because investors are showing interest does not mean any deal will happen. The distinction between an outright acquisition and an investment is central to the speculation. The reported approaches do not establish that NASCAR has received a formal takeover bid or started a sale process. Instead, they point towards businesses exploring minority ownership opportunities or joint ventures. Both could bring outside money into the organization without necessarily changing who controls it. NASCAR's leadership is drawing a clear line in the sand as major money circles the sport. Subscribe to stay ahead of what's really driving these pivotal negotiations. This is not the first time the France family has faced questions about selling. In 2018, NASCAR reportedly engaged Goldman Sachs to explore potential investment and ownership options. NBCUniversal emerged as a serious prospective buyer, with discussions involving a possible minority stake. However, the proposed transaction never materialized after parent company Comcast shifted its attention towards acquiring Sky. The France family ultimately retained control. The renewed interest is understandable when NASCAR’s commercial position is considered. Its seven-year media rights agreements, running from 2025 through 2031, involve FOX, NBC, Amazon’s Prime Video, and TNT Sports. The reported value of the Cup Series and Xfinity Series agreements is approximately $7.7 billion, providing a substantial long-term revenue foundation. Few American sports properties can offer investors that kind of established broadcasting business. NASCAR also has an important advantage in its ownership of a significant portfolio of racing venues. Its 2019 acquisition of International Speedway Corporation brought the two businesses together, giving NASCAR greater control over its tracks and the commercial opportunities surrounding them. Beyond race-day ticket sales, those properties offer potential for hospitality, entertainment, real estate development, and other events. An investor interested in unlocking that value might prefer a joint venture over purchasing the entire organization. There is another reason outside capital could appeal to NASCAR. Private equity has already found its way into the team ownership landscape. Trackhouse Racing, for instance, brought in Avenue Sports Fund, led by former Milwaukee Bucks co-owner Marc Lasry, through a significant minority investment in 2024. That transaction demonstrated the appetite for motorsports investments, although buying into a racing team is fundamentally different from acquiring an interest in the sanctioning body. The financial case for accepting an investor is therefore straightforward. NASCAR could unlock some of its considerable enterprise value while bringing in capital to strengthen its international presence, improve digital distribution, and develop its commercial properties. A strategic partner could also provide expertise in areas where the sport has room to grow. The France family would potentially benefit financially without necessarily relinquishing control. However, selling would introduce complications that go beyond ownership percentages. NASCAR’s relationship with its teams has been under considerable strain, particularly following the antitrust dispute involving 23XI Racing and Front Row Motorsports. The December 2025 settlement introduced evergreen charters and ended a prolonged legal battle over the sport’s commercial structure. Although the agreement provided greater long-term security for teams, its financial terms remained confidential. Any prospective investor would inherit those relationships and the responsibility of maintaining a sustainable business for all stakeholders. Formula One offers a useful comparison. Liberty Media completed its acquisition of the championship in 2017, in a transaction valuing the business at approximately $8 billion. Under its ownership, F1 placed greater emphasis on digital engagement, social media, international expansion, and reaching younger audiences. Netflix’s Drive to Survive subsequently helped introduce the championship to a broader American audience. The transformation demonstrated how a new ownership group could approach motorsports as a global entertainment property rather than simply a racing championship. But NASCAR cannot simply replicate that model. Formula One operates on a global calendar, while NASCAR’s identity and commercial strength remain deeply connected to the American market. Liberty’s investment also does not establish that a sale would automatically deliver similar results for NASCAR. A new controlling owner could bring fresh ideas, but pressure to maximize returns might also influence decisions involving ticket prices, scheduling, venue development, and the sport’s relationship with its teams. That is ultimately what makes O’Donnell’s position important. NASCAR can entertain investment proposals, explore commercial partnerships, and assess opportunities without putting the entire organization on the market. Investor interest is not the same as an acquisition agreement, and the France family has little reason to surrender control simply because outside businesses see potential in the sport. The question is no longer whether NASCAR is valuable enough to attract serious investment. Its media contracts, venues, and commercial reach have already established that. The bigger question is whether outside capital can make the sport more valuable without compromising the control and independence the France family has maintained since 1948. For now, O’Donnell’s message leaves little room for interpreting investor interest as an indication that NASCAR is preparing to sell. item.title: If Mikel Arteta’s dossier is part of a deliberate strategy, it is a dangerous one for Arsenal | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.” Continue reading...

Leeds were playing well, certainly better than Bournemouth for the first 30 minutes until James Trafford committed his grievous error. The goalkeeper made a horrible mess of a pass to an unwitting Ao Tanaka. In stole Justin Kluivert to set up Evanilson for a fifth goal in six matches. Where Leeds’s confidence sagged, Evanilson continued to find the best form of his time on the south coast. “I just met him and told him you are a real No 9,” Marco Rose said of the Brazilian who was full of intelligent movement. “He has to reward himself with goals and that is what he is doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I’m not here to be liked’: Glasner defiant as Brentford capitalise on Forest woes
item.description: For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest, the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”. “For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation that the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ayari on target as Brighton stun Manchester City to close gap on leaders
item.description: Manchester City have lost two consecutive league games, but no alarm should be sounded. Enzo Maresca’s fast-passing team were defeated on Saturday because Yasin Ayari took one of Brighton’s rare chances, the 11th-minute winner deriving from what appeared a wrongly awarded free-kick for Elliot Anderson’s foul on Ayari. Brighton can be proud of victory here – and of being third. They are worth the lofty position and who would bet against Champions League qualification? They protected their lead admirably because City kept coming at them: City’s problem was the final touch or finish and not creating enough for the lethal Erling Haaland. Continue reading...

item.title: Michael Carrick insists he will still be in charge of Manchester United against Roma
item.description: Defeat against Chelsea extends winless run to nine games Carrick clinging on to job after club’s worst run since 1988 Michael Carrick insisted he would still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. United’s problems mounted as their winless run reached nine games . Carrick is clinging on to his job after overseeing the club’s first such run since 1988 and tried to focus on the next game as he analysed his side’s defending when Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Chelsea. “It’s never a good goal to concede,” he said. “Morgan went through the middle of us and at that point the game was right in the balance. To concede like that was a big moment. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.” Continue reading...

item.title: No big deal: how Mac Allister shook off contract doubts to fire Liverpool’s revival
item.description: Iraola’s midfield has rediscovered its aggression and intensity just in time for Sunday’s visit of Arsenal to Anfield Alexis Mac Allister found himself in a strong position to apply pressure on Liverpool over a new contract before Atlético Madrid’s visit to Anfield last month , although only in the physical sense of being up on stage to preview the game in front of a mass audience. In reality, the 27-year-old’s negotiating stance was relatively weak. And in fairness to the Argentina international, he has been true to his word in flipping the narrative in his favour ever since. As the past two Premier League champions prepare to meet at Anfield on Sunday, when Liverpool can narrow the gap on Arsenal to three points with a fourth successive home win in all competitions, Mac Allister’s form encapsulates the impressive improvement of Andoni Iraola’s team. He has become the indispensable part of Liverpool’s central midfield and to an extent that, merely seven weeks on from that headline-grabbing Champions League press conference, it is not only Mac Allister who thinks he deserves a contract extension. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “ a breach of club discipline ”. Continue reading...

item.title: Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage champions
item.description: Ballon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clash As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club’s Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or on Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday, two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d’Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, “awesome for the WSL”. From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‑and‑a‑half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world’s best player has helped change the mindset of everyone at the club. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Roster rifts, police raids and Son’s uncertain future leave South Korea at a crossroads
item.description: After a disaster World Cup, the team have continued to spiral, with tensions high between young and older players and the captain’s standing in question Son Heung-min and Cristiano Ronaldo are iconic No 7s, Premier League legends and international record-breakers. Now there is a surprising danger of them having something else in common: being a divisive presence in their national teams. On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Rodman rule has been revised but the fight to keep stars in the NWSL goes on | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Gone are the eight criteria to be a High Impact Player so clubs can spend their money on whomever they want – and the solution makes sense When Washington plays Chicago this Sunday in DC, “Rowdy Audi” will probably be full. It will also be full when the post-season starts, should they lock up their top-four position with a positive result on Decision Day. Equipped with an accessible stadium in a big city, a proud fanbase and a formidable roster rife with players qualifying for the High Impact Player (HIP) rule’s initial criteria (including Trinity Rodman, who gave the rule its moniker), the Spirit hold sway in the attendance charts. But starting next season, everyone on the Spirit will qualify for the “Rodman Rule” . So will every player in NWSL. Announced Friday, NWSL settled a grievance with the league’s Players Association, who argued that the initial criteria violated federal labor law. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Fleetwood go their own way to down Arsenal and live Carabao Cup dream
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Having made a passing reference to Mick Fleetwood in Tuesday’s thrilling edition of your favourite email, Football Daily genuinely wasn’t expecting to be repeatedly typing that particular F-word in our lead story in today’s edition. While we were aware Arsenal were in the coastal town of Fleetwood for a Fizzy Cup tie that could scarcely have been less glamorous than the previous evening’s Ballon d’Or ceremony at the Palladium, the needle on our patented Potential Shock-o-Meter had barely moved before a match pitting the Premier League champions against a side struggling in League Two. Even with the residual winds from Storm Boelo still buffeting the ground, we presumed Arsenal’s second string would have enough about them to record a comfortable win at Highbury, over 20 years after they left a London stadium of the same name to begin their residency at the Emirates. It was not to be and almost five months to the day since exiting a cup competition on penalties following a curiously flat and uninspired display, Mikel Arteta’s side exited a cup competition on penalties following etc, and so on. Continue reading...

item.description: Plus: the longest home droughts, pre-Christmas goal centuries and the first official club websites Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Justin Seven-Seven came on in the 75th minute and then scored in the 77th minute for West Brom Under-21s against Sutton United in the National League Cup. You have probably already guessed my question, but has anyone else ever scored in the same minute as their name?” wonders Peter Skilton. Readers of a certain age may recall Didier Six , the mercurial French winger who had a brief spell at Aston Villa in 1984-85. A number of you mentioned some or all of the following sixth-minute goals, which includes two in consecutive seasons against Bordeaux: Valenciennes 2-1 Nancy (agg: 2-3) Coupe de France quarter-final, 1975-76 Valenciennes 3-2 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1976-77 Lens 2-0 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1977-78 VfB Stuttgart 5-1 Karlsruher Bundesliga, 1981-82 Bundesliga 71 goals in 18 games Champions League 18 goals in 6 games DFB-Pokal 10 goals in 3 games Franz Beckenbauer Supercup 2 goals in 1 game Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
item.description: Video appears to show Mao Zedong called a ‘dictator’ Dongpeng and Mengniu end deals with the player Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe
item.content:encoded: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Shola Ameobi: ‘I thought: how can I be most useful to Newcastle? Then the cog started turning’
item.description: From experiencing racism growing up in Newcastle to becoming a derby hero and now a member of the executive team, the former striker has been on a remarkable journey “There were times where I feared for my life as a kid, being harassed and chased by different groups of people,” Shola Ameobi says. “There were situations where I had to sprint to get away from groups of lads who didn’t like me because of what I looked like.” Ameobi is recalling growing up in Newcastle during the late 1980s and 1990s, having moved from Nigeria aged six. There were lots of moments like that. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
